newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks ignore Greenspan's U.S. rate comments.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks ignore Greenspan's U.S. rate comments.

text.p: Asian markets on Thursday shrugged off U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning of possible higher interest rates to close mostly higher.

Those that fell generally did so for domestic reasons and shrugged off Greenspan's comments to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday that the U.S. central bank might take a pre-emptive shot at fighting inflation.
Most Asian markets followed Wall Street's lead and headed lower at the opening, but the herd instinct which usually grips markets after a Greenspan speech, failed to take hold.

"The market is not collapsing," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage in Hong Kong. "I think there has been an expectation for some time that Greenspan is itching to find an excuse to put rates up."
The Hang Seng Index rose 4.77 points to close at 13,546.60 after spending most of the day in negative territory.
"People see Greenspan's comments as more smoke than fire. He has said this before and only had a really short-term effect on market," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225-share index ended up 30.64 points, or 0.16 percent, at 19,021.56 after dropping 108 points earlier.

"Tokyo is more concerned about domstic factors such as how the stock market will end the fiscal year in March than in indirect, external factors such as the Greenspan comments," said Credit Lyonnais Securities' strategist Shinichi Ichikawa.
In an uncharacteristically blunt forecast, Greenspan reiterated a warning he made in December about an "irrational exuberance" among stock and bond investors.
But brokers in Taiwan said Greenspan's comments were not expected to have any effect on the local market, which is currently dominated by bullish domestic factors.
Taiwan's bourse soared by 1.31 percent or 101.58 points to close at 7,832.07.

"Taiwan's market right now is completely dominated by local factors because of the strength of its economy. Investors are not paying any attention to what happens in the U.S. or anywhere else," said Eric Liu, analyst for National Securities.

Australia was the exception, with brokers saying Sydney's all ordinaries index was weighed down by Greenspan's comments. It shed 18.4 points to close at 2,464.70, just off its intra-day low of 2,464.40.
"In summary, the market generally followed the Dow lower after some cautionary statements from Greenspan," said John Featherby, a dealer at Perth brokerage Hartley Poynton Ltd.
Malaysian shares closed lower after profit-taking erased early modest gains, but brokers said it was a temporary setback. The Composite Index ended 5.93 ppoints lower at 1,259.4.

Singapore's Straits Times Index stumbled 25.44 points lower to close at 2,190.63, while Thai stocks fell sharply, closing 13.81 points or 1.87 percent to 726.01 on fears about the health of finance companies.
Korean stocks closed 10.30 points lower at 669.41 on rumours of financial difficulties at Sammi Corp.

A Sammi executive denied the company was in financial trouble. He said the company had missed the first deadline for debt repayments two days ago, but added the firm was able to make up for it the next day.
Indonesian stocks closed lower on selling of blue chips after briefly touching a record high of 717.47 points. The composite index closed off 2.69 points at 709.92.
One analyst said the fall was technical, but another said some investors might be squaring their positions after Greenspan's interest rate warning.
New Zealand share prices ended weaker, but brokers said the decline was led by extreme volatility in leading stock Telecom rather than Wall Street's 55-point fall.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 15.96 points down at 2,274.19 on high turnover of NZ$100 million, Telecom accounting for about three quarters of that.
Trading in the Philippines was suspended after 18 minutes due to a computer breakdown. The market was subsequently closed with the composite index off 14.40 points at 3,335.42.
